implementation_notes: Modern default in the JVM mainstream: FilterChainProxy runs an ordered SecurityFilterChain of filters - context loading, CSRF and headers, authentication filters, AuthorizationFilter - for every request before the DispatcherServlet reaches the action, so the shared security sequence is enforced by the framework rather than by a base class. Application-specific shared steps (tenant resolution, audit stamping) are added as custom filters at a documented position. The classic base action is unnecessary for the standard checks in this stack.
pitfalls: A security filter declared as a Spring bean is also auto-registered with the servlet container, so it may run twice and in an unexpected order; disable the container registration when adding it to the chain.
AuthorizationFilter must run after the authentication filters; a custom filter placed with addFilterBefore/addFilterAfter changes the sequence and can pre-empt or weaken the standard checks.
SecurityContextHolder state is thread-local and cleared per request by the framework; capturing it on a background thread loses or leaks the identity.

variants.name: Jakarta Servlet filter chain
variants.implementation_notes: Portable servlet-container realization: a filter mapped to the application's URL space wraps the whole dispatch path and runs the shared checks before calling chain.doFilter, which reaches the servlet or action only afterwards. Choose this for plain Servlet/JSP stacks or non-Spring frameworks; the filter chain replaces the base action and works in any container, but it sees only the transport-level request, not framework action metadata.
pitfalls: A filter that is not mapped to all URL patterns leaves part of the surface unguarded; verify the mapping and the dispatcher types (REQUEST, FORWARD, ERROR).
The container may invoke filters in declaration order across the descriptor and annotations; pin the order and test it.

variants.name: Abstract base Action with a template execute() (classic J2EE)
variants.idiom_name: abstract ActionSupport base with a final execute() and an abstract business step
variants.implementation_notes: The pattern's literal J2EE form: every Action extends a secure base action whose final execute() runs the shared sequence - or coordinates the framework's enforcers - and then calls an abstract business method. Keep it when maintaining a framework that dispatches to action classes with an execute/perform contract, or when the shared checks fall outside any framework interception model; the pattern's own source documents this structure.
pitfalls: Final execute() plus protected abstract step is the contract; making execute() overridable reintroduces per-action security logic.
Framework dispatch that instantiates actions directly can bypass the base if the framework's own configuration is not routed through it.
